children: The pace in which winter grains are being planted in Russia is at its slowest in over a decade, says SovEcon in a note. The firm says that Russian farmers have planted 6.1 million hectares of winter grains as of the end of last week, which is down from 7.1 million hectares at this time last year. Slowing down planting this year is "severe financial pressure amid disrupted Black Sea exports," says SovEcon. The last time planting has been this slow is in 2013, when an unusually wet season interrupted the planting campaign, says the firm. At its current pace, planting is off 25% from the five-year average, says SovEcon. Most-active CBOT wheat futures are down 1.4%. (kirk.maltais@wsj.com)
